speaker: mayonprovenzano
text: So I wanna welcome everybody to our budget meeting, our first budget meeting of 2020. Before I asked the clerk to begin the meeting, there were two things I wanted to do. The first is a request, and the second is a recognition. With respect to the request, I've noted recently on social media, a lot of understandable kind of activity around the Christmas season, where people are going to Christmas parties and socializing with one another. And although I understand why this is occurring, I really wanna kind of take the opportunity to ask the community to refrain from social gatherings with people outside of your own household in closed door settings. I think we now know that one of the most significant COVID risks are when people from different households get together at an indoor setting and spend time together in close proximity to one another. We saw a spike in our cases post Halloween, and I expect that if we continue to socialize in a significant way with one another outside of our households, or those people who live outside of our households, we'll see another increase in our cases. I think it's critically important to keep the kids in our community safe, all the kids that we have in daycare and in schools, and all the seniors in our community safe, all the people that are living in retirement homes and each other safe, that we follow public health advice. And public health is asking us to minimize socialization outside of our own households. They're asking us to wear a mask when we're indoors with people that are not in our own households. They're asking us to keep physically distance from people that we do not reside with when we're out and about. And it's hard to do those things if we gather for holiday gatherings over the holiday season. So I'd ask the community, even though it's a significant sacrifice, to make the sacrifice this holiday season. Hopefully by next holiday season, we'll be able to spend a lot of time together, and we will be well past this and have a lot to celebrate. As for the acknowledgement, I think we are all aware now that on the weekend, we lost Ron Irwin. Ron was a giant in our community. He was a really interesting man who led a very interesting life, and he loved Sault Ste. Marie dearly. And there are very few people born and raised in the west end of our city, or really born and raised in any part of our city, who traveled the path that Ron traveled. He held a lot of different offices, and he served our community and our country well for decades. So I wanted to take the moment to recognize his contribution, to thank him and his family for his contribution, and to say to Marg and his children and his grandchildren that we appreciate Ron and his service, and we appreciate the significant loss that they are currently dealing with, and that they have our deepest and most sincerest condolences as they work through this loss. Ron will be missed by many of us, and he will be missed for a very long time. Madam Clerk, if you can please start the meeting.
